points.text: Dataset has little novelty: pooled existing samples labelled by existing open models.
Labelling ignores compositional text-image effects where joint label differs from modalities.
No notion of harmful-topic inputs that do not seek harmful responses.
Merging Child and Animal Abuse into one category poorly motivated.
No human inter-annotator agreement or auto-label vs human alignment reported.
Cleaning and human annotation details (annotators, backgrounds, guidelines) omitted.
Training set fully auto-labelled with no quality control.
Contribution incremental: aggregation, auto-labelling, small test set, fine-tuning.
Limited novelty; no original data, scenario or annotation methodology.
Class imbalance for rare categories hurts accuracy; no mitigation.
Accuracy only; no precision, recall, F1 or multiple seeds.
No quantitative annotation reliability metric.
Data curation relies on MLLMs, capping quality by their capability.
FalconEye weak on fine-grained category classification.
In-domain test makes comparison unfair; out-of-domain performance unclear.
Claims of outperforming all baselines misworded; no table includes all baselines.
Teacher-student in-distribution confound; teacher not evaluated, baseline prompts unstated.
No annotator information or agreement; accuracy ceiling unknown.
Cross-modal thesis untested; text-only guards close.
Split unit, validation and checkpoint selection unstated; shared prompt-image pairs.
Accuracy only on skewed labels; baseline near majority rate; need F1/MCC/CIs.
Main-text category subset selectively favourable.
Realism claim inconsistent with >80% harmful instructions.
Cross-reference error, duplicate row, 'FalconEye-test' typo.
Baseline below 50% suggests prompt/parsing mismatch.
Headline claim stronger than tables: tiny margins, category deficit, incomplete baselines.
Dataset documentation missing: train size, split, per-category counts, cleaning counts.
Human annotator details and agreement missing.
Main text hides unfavourable category results.
Realism claim about harmful proportion inconsistent.
Minor cross-reference, typo, duplicate row, caption style.
Training silver labels from 72B model with no human agreement check.
Test annotation process undocumented; no inter-annotator agreement.
Baseline matrix incomplete across tables; 'outperforms all' not demonstrated.
Teacher labeller not evaluated; no control fine-tuned on existing safety data.
Accuracy only on imbalanced labels, small margins, no CIs.
Split and selection protocol unstated; prompt-image overlap risk.
Cross-modal advantage untested: no image ablation or cross-modal subset.
Rationale/explanation quality never evaluated.
Category detection weak and deficit vs GPT-4o understated.
Single-4090 efficiency claim lacks latency/memory numbers.
Minor: duplicate row, number formatting, naming typos.
LlavaGuard and MLLMGuard neither cited nor compared.
Delta over source datasets not isolated; Table 1 mixes dataset and evaluator, omits BeaverTails-V.
Taxonomy merging choices asserted without validation; broad categories.
Claims about Llama-Guard-Vision limits and prior datasets' coverage untested.
AdvBench and BeaverTails-V citations questionable.
No ethics, access-control or annotator-welfare discussion for harmful dataset.
Harm treated as single universal label despite contested normative judgements.
External benchmark performance well below in-distribution.
No audit-relevant metrics or actual MLLM auditing study.
Judge robustness to other model responses and adversarial images unexamined.
Only image-text experiments despite mentioning audio/video.

P.summary: Limited novelty: dataset aggregated from existing sources.
No category for harmful-topic but benign-intent inputs.
Human annotation process and agreement unreported.

Q.summary: In-distribution teacher-student confound; missing teacher and control fine-tune.
Accuracy-only on imbalanced labels; no CIs.
Delta over source datasets not isolated.
No audit metrics or auditing study.
Judge robustness to distribution shift/adversarial images.
